title: I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4)
summary: After a break (a Europe trip, moving across the country with his gym, a new job) and passing 100K subscribers, he shows a back-and-arms day from his old gym in two giant sets. He explains his loop pinwheel curls for the brachioradialis, alternating neutral and croc dumbbell rows around dips, pullover-then-sit-up pairing, and rest-pause EZ-bar preacher curls.
claims: He went quiet for a while because of a trip to Europe, a move across the country with his whole gym and a new job; the channel passed 100K subscribers
A back day of six lat exercises is stupid; he trains back hard alongside arms or alongside chest and shoulders
His warm-up is just the day's movements with lighter weight, with no stretching
This year he is prioritising the brachioradialis and forearms, which are his weak points, over the biceps
Take every isolation movement to failure: it's free volume, and you won't get hurt unless you're careless
Open an arm day with a movement you enjoy, and include other body parts, since arms-only days lead to junk volume such as 6-7 triceps exercises on bro splits
He does only 3-4 sets of direct brachioradialis work per session, with maximum intent
On dumbbell rows some body English to start the lift is fine, but never cheat the negative, which is where most of the gains are
Pristine bodybuilding form can leave you lifting baby weight; slightly ego-lifting with a bit more weight and a better stretch can be better for hypertrophy
Bodyweight calisthenics eventually stops progressing; once he could do 20 dips with 10 lb ankle weights it was time for weighted calisthenics
Goofiness, such as dancing between sets, is anabolic

You can superset a back row with itself using a different grip if another muscle's exercise sits in between: first the variation for the weaker muscle (neutral row for lats), then the one for the stronger muscle (croc row for traps)
Grip changes the elbow angle and therefore how the back is hit: neutral-grip dumbbell rows favour the lats, pronated croc rows the traps
This double-row trick works for horizontal rows but probably not for pull-ups, where performance would suffer
Compounds tolerate more sets than small isolation muscles (6 sets of rows and dips vs 3 of curls), so feed small muscles volume through a wide selection of slightly different angles
His ribcage has grown enough from heavy dumbbell pullovers to make his 36-inch waist look small
Pullovers before sit-ups give the abs a pre-stimulus, not pre-fatigue: they are stretched but keep their strength
You can keep a six-pack all year without being very lean by training abs constantly: at least one ab exercise of 3 sets on every chest, shoulder or arm day
The close-grip EZ-bar preacher curl is the best biceps exercise and is safe when done right
Rest-pause on preacher curls: at failure rest 10-30 s, do a slow negative and explode up, repeat; it often adds 50% more reps and reaches true failure, but it is for advanced lifters only
exercises: Loop pinwheel curl
strap loop near the thumb and wrist, curl across the body, pronate on the way up and supinate on the way down, never lock out, slow negative, to failure
brachioradialis and forearms more than biceps; the supination gives a biceps stretch
Dumbbell row (neutral)
hand on bench, torso near horizontal, let the dumbbell rotate into the body to stretch the lats, rest-pause for extra reps; straps optional
lats; standing more upright makes it easier but hits lats less
Triceps dip
torso vertical, stop slightly below parallel
more triceps than chest
Croc row (pronated dumbbell row)
pronated grip after the neutral rows, with dips between
hits traps harder
Dumbbell pullover
hips low, controlled range, don't let the dumbbell go far behind the head
stretches the back in a different direction; overextending the shoulder disengages the lats and risks injury; expands the ribcage
Sit-up
after pullovers
abs pre-stimulated by the pullover stretch
Close-grip EZ-bar preacher curl
pad not too steep, shoulders back, stop with forearm parallel to the floor or slightly below, rest-pause at failure
best biceps movement; going too deep rolls the shoulders forward and risks overextending the biceps
training_log: bodyweight plus 10 lb ankle weights; easily 20 reps
